Commentary: Taijul Islam to Kavem Hodge, FOUR, Kavem Hodge in the mood to finish it off early. It's tossed up full and he comes down the track, gets too close to the pitch, but drills the drive and beats the dive of mid-off to his right
Taijul Islam to Kavem Hodge, 1 run, good length on off and middle, Kavem Hodge goes on the back foot and cuts hard and straight to deep extra-cover

Taijul Islam to Brandon King, no run, slower and on a good length on off, bit of extra bounce, Brandon King handles it well as he angles the defence to the right of slip. Played with soft hands and down
Taijul Islam to Brandon King, 1 run, fired full outside off, Brandon King gets forward to push to the right of backward point for one
Nayeem Hasan to Brandon King, no run, tossed up on a good length and turns in sharply, Brandon King gets forward to defend, it hits the thick inside edge and rolls away to his right

Nayeem Hasan to Brandon King, no run, wow! Big turn and bounce. Rips from outside off and lands on a length, comes into middle, Brandon King goes on the back foot to flick, hit on the back leg high. Easily going over and Litton Das tells Nayeem Hasan to get on with it
Nayeem Hasan to Brandon King, 1 run, flat good length just outside off, Brandon King goes on the back foot and pulls hard and straight to deep mid-wicket
Nayeem Hasan to Kavem Hodge, 1 run, good length on off, Kavem Hodge goes on the back foot and pulls to deep mid-wicket
Nayeem Hasan to Brandon King, 1 run, good length and turns into off and middle, Brandon King goes on the back foot and nudges it to long-on
Nayeem Hasan to Kavem Hodge, no run, caught at slip but no bat or glove. It's tossed up full outside off, bit of bounce beats the attempted sweep of Kavem Hodge, off the right arm and to slip

Taijul Islam to Brandon King, FOUR, "this victory is tremendous" is the comment from Ian Bishop on air. Flat good length around off, Brandon King goes on the back foot and forces it hard, has to beat a packed off-side field and does so through extra-cover. Fittingly King finishes it off. Celebrations begin in the West Indies camp as they are all smiles and congratulating each other. Chase so happy as soon as the winning runs were scored. King and Kavem Hodge hug as the post-match formalities follow

15:56 Local Time, 09:56 GMT, 15:26 IST: A special win for West Indies this. They don't often win abroad and that too so convincingly. 170 was supposed to test them but the openers set them on their way with a 112-run stand and that made the task easier. Bangladesh were not allowed to settle as Campbell and King both decided to play attacking cricket. They didn't allow the spinners to cause any impact as the trio went wicketless. That should disappoint Bangladesh a lot on a surface which helped them on day 4. Earlier in the day, Bangladesh started on 79/6 and were bowled out for 142 with Nayeem Hasan making 52. Chase and Warrican were outstanding sharing 9 wickets between themselves. One expected West Indies to not saunter to victory as they did eventually, with only bad light and lightning preventing them from reaching there much earlier.

Match summary: Bangladesh won the toss and opted to bat first. They made 272 with Shadman making 105. Bangladesh lost their last 7 wickets for 51 runs slipping from 221/3 to 272 all-out. Warrican the star with a fifer. In reply, West Indies made 245 with 50s from Campbell, Chanderpaul, and 40s from Greaves and Chase. Nayeem wrapped up things with a four-fer. With a 27-run lead behind them, Bangladesh slipped to 53/6 as Chase starred with the ball with able support from Warrican. Bad light and some dogged resistance from Nayeem and Jaker Ali (the concussion sub for Mominul) prevented more damage to Bangladesh yesterday. The game was lost to a large extent by Bangladesh in that phase yesterday when Chase and Warrican spun a web. From 53/6, Bangladesh did well to reach 142 but 170 was easily chased down by West Indies as the openers shone. Stay tuned for the post-match stuff....

Chase 2/2: [On his own bowling performance, his improvement in the second innings, and taking five wickets to help restrict Bangladesh to a chaseable total.] Yeah, I'm pleased with the performance in the second innings because I didn't have the best of performances with the ball in the first innings. So the guys really asked me to give themselves in the second innings with the ball and challenged me. So I tried to put my hand up and I got five wickets and it helped us to restrict them for a low total, a low enough total that we could have chased in the second innings on a pitch that was offering a bit. But I still thought that it was a good cricket wicket.

We will leave it there. The 2nd Test of the series is on 5th November in Sylhet. Interesting to see what kind of pitch is offered there. We will be there nice and early for that one. Do join us then.
